sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Perlica is a 5 -star character in Arknights: Endfield (AKE). Perlica wields an Arts Unit and belongs to the Caster class. Perlica also has access to the Electric element. This guide provides a comprehensive overview of Perlica 's best build, including recommended Weapons, Gear pieces, Stats, and the strongest team compositions and rotations that maximize their potential.

 To learn more about Perlica check the sections below. Use the tabs to quickly switch to the kind of information you're looking for - whether it's best build, teams, synergies or calculations.

sections.heading: Lore
sections.text:
"We once fought on and never gave up ... for it is our wish to witness your return."
 Perlica is the Supervisor of Endfield Industries and the official spokesperson of the company. She is primarily responsible for overseeing and advancing the development and application of Protocol-Originium technology, while also managing the operations of Dijiang.
 As an outstanding expert in Techno-Protocol, she guided research that had a key influence on the adaptive development and application of the technology, and helped refine the Automated Industry Complex (AIC Factory).
 She is capable of responding to various crises in a calm and decisive manner. However, Endfield often faces challenges that go beyond all expectations. While the Endministrator was in hibernation, she took command of the Crisis Team, leading the heroes of Endfield Industries in a battle for a greater cause. Perlica moves tirelessly across the Civilization Band, doing whatever she can to maintain order and keep things running.

sections.heading: Pros
sections.text:
Can forcibly apply Electrification for free with Combo Skill, boosting all Arts damage taken.

 Can freely apply Electric Infliction quickly with the Battle Skill.

 Above-average personal damage output for the support damage role.

 Many viable, supportive weapon choices further boost support damage capabilities.

 Incredibly easy to trigger Combo Skill usable in any team.

 Might not always be optimal, but works in every Arts Damage-based team thanks to her generic combo and debuff.

 She's free!

sections.heading: Cons
sections.text: Without potentials combo, Electrification has a low duration, which must be timed during large damage moments to get value out of.

sections.heading: Kit Intro
sections.text:
Perlica is a 5-star, Electric, Arts Unit support damage dealer who specializes in forcibly applying Electrification without the need to consume any Arts Inflictions or spend any SP thanks to her Combo Skill. Said Combo Skill is also exceptionally easy to trigger, only requiring the controlled operator to land a Final Strike. This, combined with the fact that the Electrification she applies causes enemies to take extra Arts damage from all major elements except Physical, means it’s always viable to slot Perlica into any Arts damage-based team as long as you time her Combo Skill to trigger right before the team's major burst damage.
 On top of her flexible Combo Skill, Perlica also has solid damage output herself thanks to a combination of good multipliers across her main skills. Another point of versatility is her ability to play into either Arts reactions or Electric burst with the Electric Infliction of her Battle Skill. You can choose to invest SP into her, or not; either option is viable depending on the team's requirements.
 Last but not least, Perlica gains a large boost to her supportive capabilities due to her weapon type being Arts Units. There are multiple very strong options Perlica can use to buff herself or the team, further solidifying her value as either a sub DPS or capable supporter of the compositions she plays within.

sections.heading: Combo
sections.text:
Perlica’s Combo Skill is the cornerstone of her kit and a large part of the reason to bring her to many teams. It has a decently long cooldown but only requires the controlled operator to perform a Final Strike on an enemy to trigger, which is very easy to fulfill. Using the Combo skill deals Electric damage, some Stagger, and forcibly applies Electrification to the target while ignoring all Arts Inflictions present on the enemy. At base, the forced Electrification has the effect of a 1 Infliction Electrification, but with a much shorter duration of 5 seconds. The forced Electrification also does not deal any direct damage.
 Note: Because the Combo Skill ignores other Inflictions and reactions on the enemy, Perlica can use it without interrupting mono-element teams that would otherwise not be able to access the reaction consistently.
 Tip: Despite being forcibly applied, Art's Intensity still affects the Infliction from Perlica’s Combo Skill, improving the stats value in teams that value the damage taken of this debuff highly.

sections.heading: Battle Skill
sections.text: Perlica’s Battle Skill is less universally useful in most teams, but still worth considering in others, depending on the Inflictions or reactions you’re after. Using it requires the usual 100 SP, deals some Electric damage, Stagger, and applies Electric Infliction to enemies hit. When building Perlica around Arts Intensity to maximize her Electrification debuff, the up-front damage this Battle Skill can deal through Arts burst and reactions can become quite significant in some teams, making it more valuable than it may appear at first glance.

sections.heading: Ultimate
sections.text: Perlica’s Ultimate is as simple as abilities come; it costs 80 to use, deals a high multiplier hit of Electric damage in an area, and some Stagger. Usually best when saved to be used during enemy Stagger windows to take advantage of one of Perlica’s talents — it should also be aligned to hit while the enemy is suffering from Electrification to increase its damage. The only other nuance to using this ability is the fact that using it can trigger some Arts Units' passives, some of which buff the team, so you may want to align it before other high-burst abilities.

sections.heading: Talents
sections.text:
Perlica’s talents aren’t transformational but can yield some nice bonuses. The first, Obliteration Protocol, is the more generic of the two and increases damage dealt to Staggered enemies by +30%, which is the same stat as DMG% vs Staggered, and stacks additively with stats like Electric DMG%. This is a nice boost that encourages the use of large abilities like Perlica’s Ultimate during Stagger windows.
 Perlica’s other talent, Cycle Protocol, causes her Combo Skill to chain to another enemy when used against an enemy with Vulnerable on them. This chain allows her to hit and afflict two enemies with her combo instead of the usual one. Perlica can sometimes find herself in teams with Vulnerability stacks, but it’s definitely not common, as those teams are usually focused around Physical damage, which Perlica isn’t able to synergize well with. Because of that, this talent is on the more niche side.

sections.heading: Gameplay
sections.text:
Perlica’s gameplay changes depending on the team you’re playing her in, but here are some general guidelines you can follow and work around as a base:
 Time Perlica’s Combo Skill for before high damage scenarios in teams that bring her for her Electrification debuff.

 Use Perlica’s Ultimate while Electrification is applied and ideally during Stagger. When using an Arts Unit that buffs the team after activating Ultimate, align its use to be before allies' major burst abilities, but still during Electrification.

 Manage Perlica’s Combo Skill cooldown so you don’t lose out on activations by holding it unnecessarily, but also ensure you don’t use it too early that expires before you deal the majority of your damage.

 If your team requires Electric Infliction, use Perlica’s Battle Skill as needed.

 Tip: In teams that use Electrification for other purposes, like Arts reaction consumption teams, including characters like Arclight or Wulfgard, you can be more liberal with deploying Perlica’s Combo Skill to maximize total consumptions in a fight.

sections.heading: Best Weapons
sections.text:
Perlica best Weapons are placed in order of what fits their playstyle the most . Check the comments to get additional context.

 1

 Stanza of Memorials (P 5 )

 Best general support weapon in non-Electric teams, Stanza has reasonable passive stats for Perlica, but more importantly it grants all non-Electric operator a sizable ATK increase after Perlica uses her Ultimate. With this weapon, aim to use Perlica's Ultimate before your main burst window.

 2

 Detonation Unit (P 0 )

 As Stanza does not work with Electric operators, Detonation Unit is a strong support option in Electric teams assuming you can trigger Electric Bursts with Perlica's Battle Skill. When doing so it will apply a strong Arts DMG Taken debuff. Outside of its team capabilities, the offensive passives are fairly underwhelming for Perlica.

 3

 Wild Wanderer (P 5 )

 Another supportive option for Perlica with a passive dedicated to buffing Electric and Physical teams everytime Perlica uses her Combo Skill which can be easily maintained. The damage bonus from this weapon is the least potent of the buffs available on her weapons, but the excellent passive stats and ease of access makes it worth considering. If Perlica cannot easily trigger Arts Bursts for Detonation Unit, such as in teams with Zhuang Fangyi, Wild Wanderer will be her best support option.

 When using Perlica as a damage dealer, Oblivion is her best thanks to its solid passive stats and its outstanding Weapon Effect, which grants Perlica a huge amount of Arts DMG% when using her Ultimate or Combo Skill.

sections.heading: Potentials Review
sections.text:
P 1
 Crisis Handling

 Increases the duration of Perlica’s Combo Skill Electrification by 75%, upgrading its length from 5 seconds to almost 9 seconds. This potential is a huge upgrade to Perlica’s supportive potential, almost doubling the duration of one of her most impactful abilities. In teams where you aren’t triggering proper Electrification reactions with Electric Infliction, this potential is close to a must-have.

 P 2
 Negotiation Tactics

 Reduces Perlica’s Ultimate Cost by -15%, taking it from 80 energy to 6,8 improving accessibility, leading to higher total damage output and more chances at activating weapons that trigger off of Ultimate use.

 P 3
 Supervisory Duties

 After Perlica applies Electrification, she gains a +20% attack boost for 5 seconds, stacking up to 2 times. This Ability is most likely to trigger off of her combo with two stacks accessible when it chains after hitting Vulnerable enemies. Maintaining this buff long term or even reaching 2 stacks at all isn’t realistic for Perlica in most teams, but when played around correctly, you should have it for most Perlica Ultimates, as you should be aligning Electrification and her Ultimate alongside the rest of your team's burst damage, preferably during Stagger.

 P 4
 Constant Guidance

 The wording or effect on Perlica’s Potential 4 is currently incorrect - which it is, we’re not sure. What the potential actually does is upgrade the force Electrification from using a 1 Infliction Electrification as a base to a 2 Infliction instead. This elevates the damage taken debuff from 12% (before Arts intensity) to 16%. The duration of the Electrification does not change from this potential compared to P1.

 P 5
 Reentry Control

 Increases the Crit Rate of Perlica’s Ultimate by +30%. This, with 50% Crit Damage, is equivalent to a 15% total increase to Perlica’s Ultimate damage. Not a bad damage boost, but not a game-changer, and doesn’t improve her supportive capabilities at all.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
Cryo

 Last Rite Cryo

 Perlica has outstanding supportive weapon choices

 Can apply Electrification for free with Combo skill, which is easily timed to align with Last Rite's Ultimate and Combo skill, increasing damage taken by the target signifcantly

 Solid sub DPS potential, contributing a bit of damage of her own

 Works well alongside other buffers who cover other buff categories, such as Amp, DMG%, and ATK%, as Perlica's Damage Taken is in a different multiplier group

 Electric

 Arclight Electric

 Applies Electrification for free with her Combo skill, triggering Arclight's Combo skill once. Electrification can then be consumed by her Battle Skill, which triggers her Combo again, positioning Perlica as a free activator for Arclight

 Perlica has outstanding supportive weapon choices, which nicely buff Arclight and the rest of the team

 Arclight's own supportive weapon and sets buff Perlica back, allowing the two to buff each other in order to both deal more damage

 Arclight consumes minimal SP herself and generates some back, freeing it up in some teams for Perlica to use on her Battle Skill to gain more damage

 Heat

 Wulfgard Heat

 Applies Electrication with Combo Skill for free, which Wulfgard can consume with his Battle Skill to deal additional damage

 Perlica has outstanding supportive weapon choices

 Combining Electric infliction from Perlica's battle skill and heat from Wulfgard forms natural reactions of either Combustion or Electrication - both of which Wulf can consume, giving him a continual source of damage that is only limited by SP

 Physical

 Rossi Physical

 Perlica has decent personal damage and strong buffs, with easily accessible Electrification and having Stanza of Memorials as a competitive weapon option to buff Rossi's Heat DMG.

 Constant reactions and readily available Inflictions can have compounding synergies with other teammates (e.g. Gilberta Combo).

 Perlica is strictly an Arts-based support and reliant on other Operators for Combustion or Corrosion set-ups.

 Electric

 Zhuang Fangyi Electric

 Perlica is by far the most important enabler teammate for Zhuang Fangyi thanks to her free Electrification debuff from Combo Skill, which can be easily activated through Final Strikes.

 Perlica has access to a reliable Electric Infliction through her Battle Skill, which is needed to trigger Zhuang Fangyi's Combo Skill.

 She's able to buff the team through Arts Units (Wild Wanderer), and contributes a non-negligible amount of damage herself.

 On the flipside, despite having higher scaling on her Electrification's Arts DMG Taken effect, this rarely comes into play owing to Fangyi's Reaction consumption.

 Note: It's beneficial to have Perlica after Fangyi in the team order. This is because timestop interactions means that her Combo Skill will land first if both are used in quick succession. Reverse ordering can work, but would demand waiting longer before using Fangyi's Combo.

sections.heading: Extra things to look out for
sections.text:
This is also an SP friendly version, which gives up on an Arclight Combo Skill. If SP allows, then shift the rotation to happen earlier, with the addition of a Perlica Battle Skill after Arclight's Ultimate applies Forced Electrification and having the Final Strike that staggers and triggers Avywenna's and Perlica's Combo Skills happening after Arclight's Battle and Combo Skill.
 The point being that then there isn't a need to hold back on using Arclight's Battle Skill, as Avywenna's Combo Skill would be triggered by the Electric Infliction applied by Perlica as opposed to the Ultimate's forced Electrification. This would lead to a Combo Skill trigger both from Arclight's Battle Skill and Perlica's Combo Skill, instead of just one as is the case above. Antal's Combo Skill can also be delayed to do this with no SP consumption, but this would mean giving up on an Arts Burst for weapon set triggers.
 Note that the "Final Strike" here does not indicate that it is the only Final Strike, as depending on where you are in Basic Attack strings, it's likely that a Final Strike may occur between Arclight's Ultimate and the one indicated.
 It's fine if not every Electrification is consumed by Arclight's Battle Skill, as SP economy may not allow for it. So long as there are enough Battle Skills being used to fuel Avywenna's Ultimate (and there is SP left for her own Battle Skill), it's enough.
 Shifting the Finisher to the start of the stagger period can work too, as the SP recovery it provides could sustain additional Battle Skill casts to give more Ultimate Energy if required.

 Team #2

sections.heading: Team Members
sections.text:
Yvonne

 Gilberta

 Arts Unit Operators have access to some of the strongest supportive weapons in the game, so running 3 of them in a team is not only viable, it can be an optimal set-up for certain types of speedrun kills. Perlica in particular distinguishes herself by being able to provide strong buffs via her Electrification when built for Arts Intensity (which gets far stronger at P4+) and working as a Stanza wielder in the comp,
 This team can struggle in 0 Ultimate Energy start encounters, with no SP efficient way to build Inflictions outside of Gilberta's Ultimate, but for full Ultimate Energy starts or multi-phase bosses that allow one to stockpile resources (such as Marble Aggelomorai), it can be one of the most competitive burst options.
 Even then, the team still does well when properly aligning skills. On the lead-up to Yvonne's Ultimate, it's possible to use Perlica's Combo Skill alongside Gilberta's to get both full Electrification and Solidification uptime for the entire burst.  Lore

 "We once fought on and never gave up ... for it is our wish to witness your return."
 Perlica is the Supervisor of Endfield Industries and the official spokesperson of the company. She is primarily responsible for overseeing and advancing the development and application of Protocol-Originium technology, while also managing the operations of Dijiang.
 As an outstanding expert in Techno-Protocol, she guided research that had a key influence on the adaptive development and application of the technology, and helped refine the Automated Industry Complex (AIC Factory).
 She is capable of responding to various crises in a calm and decisive manner. However, Endfield often faces challenges that go beyond all expectations. While the Endministrator was in hibernation, she took command of the Crisis Team, leading the heroes of Endfield Industries in a battle for a greater cause. Perlica moves tirelessly across the Civilization Band, doing whatever she can to maintain order and keep things running.

 Review

 Kit Intro
 Perlica is a 5-star, Electric, Arts Unit support damage dealer who specializes in forcibly applying Electrification without the need to consume any Arts Inflictions or spend any SP thanks to her Combo Skill. Said Combo Skill is also exceptionally easy to trigger, only requiring the controlled operator to land a Final Strike. This, combined with the fact that the Electrification she applies causes enemies to take extra Arts damage from all major elements except Physical, means it’s always viable to slot Perlica into any Arts damage-based team as long as you time her Combo Skill to trigger right before the team's major burst damage.
 On top of her flexible Combo Skill, Perlica also has solid damage output herself thanks to a combination of good multipliers across her main skills. Another point of versatility is her ability to play into either Arts reactions or Electric burst with the Electric Infliction of her Battle Skill. You can choose to invest SP into her, or not; either option is viable depending on the team's requirements.
 Last but not least, Perlica gains a large boost to her supportive capabilities due to her weapon type being Arts Units. There are multiple very strong options Perlica can use to buff herself or the team, further solidifying her value as either a sub DPS or capable supporter of the compositions she plays within.
 Combo
 Perlica’s Combo Skill is the cornerstone of her kit and a large part of the reason to bring her to many teams. It has a decently long cooldown but only requires the controlled operator to perform a Final Strike on an enemy to trigger, which is very easy to fulfill. Using the Combo skill deals Electric damage, some Stagger, and forcibly applies Electrification to the target while ignoring all Arts Inflictions present on the enemy. At base, the forced Electrification has the effect of a 1 Infliction Electrification, but with a much shorter duration of 5 seconds. The forced Electrification also does not deal any direct damage.
 Note: Because the Combo Skill ignores other Inflictions and reactions on the enemy, Perlica can use it without interrupting mono-element teams that would otherwise not be able to access the reaction consistently.
 Tip: Despite being forcibly applied, Art's Intensity still affects the Infliction from Perlica’s Combo Skill, improving the stats value in teams that value the damage taken of this debuff highly.
 Battle Skill
 Perlica’s Battle Skill is less universally useful in most teams, but still worth considering in others, depending on the Inflictions or reactions you’re after. Using it requires the usual 100 SP, deals some Electric damage, Stagger, and applies Electric Infliction to enemies hit. When building Perlica around Arts Intensity to maximize her Electrification debuff, the up-front damage this Battle Skill can deal through Arts burst and reactions can become quite significant in some teams, making it more valuable than it may appear at first glance.
 Ultimate
 Perlica’s Ultimate is as simple as abilities come; it costs 80 to use, deals a high multiplier hit of Electric damage in an area, and some Stagger. Usually best when saved to be used during enemy Stagger windows to take advantage of one of Perlica’s talents — it should also be aligned to hit while the enemy is suffering from Electrification to increase its damage. The only other nuance to using this ability is the fact that using it can trigger some Arts Units' passives, some of which buff the team, so you may want to align it before other high-burst abilities.
 Talents
 Perlica’s talents aren’t transformational but can yield some nice bonuses. The first, Obliteration Protocol, is the more generic of the two and increases damage dealt to Staggered enemies by +30%, which is the same stat as DMG% vs Staggered, and stacks additively with stats like Electric DMG%. This is a nice boost that encourages the use of large abilities like Perlica’s Ultimate during Stagger windows.
 Perlica’s other talent, Cycle Protocol, causes her Combo Skill to chain to another enemy when used against an enemy with Vulnerable on them. This chain allows her to hit and afflict two enemies with her combo instead of the usual one. Perlica can sometimes find herself in teams with Vulnerability stacks, but it’s definitely not common, as those teams are usually focused around Physical damage, which Perlica isn’t able to synergize well with. Because of that, this talent is on the more niche side.
 Gameplay
 Perlica’s gameplay changes depending on the team you’re playing her in, but here are some general guidelines you can follow and work around as a base:
 Time Perlica’s Combo Skill for before high damage scenarios in teams that bring her for her Electrification debuff.

 Use Perlica’s Ultimate while Electrification is applied and ideally during Stagger. When using an Arts Unit that buffs the team after activating Ultimate, align its use to be before allies' major burst abilities, but still during Electrification.

 Manage Perlica’s Combo Skill cooldown so you don’t lose out on activations by holding it unnecessarily, but also ensure you don’t use it too early that expires before you deal the majority of your damage.

 If your team requires Electric Infliction, use Perlica’s Battle Skill as needed.

 Tip: In teams that use Electrification for other purposes, like Arts reaction consumption teams, including characters like Arclight or Wulfgard, you can be more liberal with deploying Perlica’s Combo Skill to maximize total consumptions in a fight.

 Potentials Review

 P 1
 Crisis Handling

 Increases the duration of Perlica’s Combo Skill Electrification by 75%, upgrading its length from 5 seconds to almost 9 seconds. This potential is a huge upgrade to Perlica’s supportive potential, almost doubling the duration of one of her most impactful abilities. In teams where you aren’t triggering proper Electrification reactions with Electric Infliction, this potential is close to a must-have.

 P 2
 Negotiation Tactics

 Reduces Perlica’s Ultimate Cost by -15%, taking it from 80 energy to 6,8 improving accessibility, leading to higher total damage output and more chances at activating weapons that trigger off of Ultimate use.

 P 3
 Supervisory Duties

 After Perlica applies Electrification, she gains a +20% attack boost for 5 seconds, stacking up to 2 times. This Ability is most likely to trigger off of her combo with two stacks accessible when it chains after hitting Vulnerable enemies. Maintaining this buff long term or even reaching 2 stacks at all isn’t realistic for Perlica in most teams, but when played around correctly, you should have it for most Perlica Ultimates, as you should be aligning Electrification and her Ultimate alongside the rest of your team's burst damage, preferably during Stagger.

 P 4
 Constant Guidance

 The wording or effect on Perlica’s Potential 4 is currently incorrect - which it is, we’re not sure. What the potential actually does is upgrade the force Electrification from using a 1 Infliction Electrification as a base to a 2 Infliction instead. This elevates the damage taken debuff from 12% (before Arts intensity) to 16%. The duration of the Electrification does not change from this potential compared to P1.

 P 5
 Reentry Control

 Increases the Crit Rate of Perlica’s Ultimate by +30%. This, with 50% Crit Damage, is equivalent to a 15% total increase to Perlica’s Ultimate damage. Not a bad damage boost, but not a game-changer, and doesn’t improve her supportive capabilities at all.

 Perlica has outstanding supportive weapon choices

 Combining Electric infliction from Perlica's battle skill and heat from Wulfgard forms natural reactions of either Combustion or Electrication - both of which Wulf can consume, giving him a continual source of damage that is only limited by SP

 Physical

 Rossi Physical

 Perlica has decent personal damage and strong buffs, with easily accessible Electrification and having Stanza of Memorials as a competitive weapon option to buff Rossi's Heat DMG.

 Constant reactions and readily available Inflictions can have compounding synergies with other teammates (e.g. Gilberta Combo).

 Perlica is strictly an Arts-based support and reliant on other Operators for Combustion or Corrosion set-ups.

 Electric

 Zhuang Fangyi Electric

 Perlica is by far the most important enabler teammate for Zhuang Fangyi thanks to her free Electrification debuff from Combo Skill, which can be easily activated through Final Strikes.

 Perlica has access to a reliable Electric Infliction through her Battle Skill, which is needed to trigger Zhuang Fangyi's Combo Skill.

 She's able to buff the team through Arts Units (Wild Wanderer), and contributes a non-negligible amount of damage herself.

 On the flipside, despite having higher scaling on her Electrification's Arts DMG Taken effect, this rarely comes into play owing to Fangyi's Reaction consumption.

 Note: It's beneficial to have Perlica after Fangyi in the team order. This is because timestop interactions means that her Combo Skill will land first if both are used in quick succession. Reverse ordering can work, but would demand waiting longer before using Fangyi's Combo.

 Extra things to look out for
 This is also an SP friendly version, which gives up on an Arclight Combo Skill. If SP allows, then shift the rotation to happen earlier, with the addition of a Perlica Battle Skill after Arclight's Ultimate applies Forced Electrification and having the Final Strike that staggers and triggers Avywenna's and Perlica's Combo Skills happening after Arclight's Battle and Combo Skill.
 The point being that then there isn't a need to hold back on using Arclight's Battle Skill, as Avywenna's Combo Skill would be triggered by the Electric Infliction applied by Perlica as opposed to the Ultimate's forced Electrification. This would lead to a Combo Skill trigger both from Arclight's Battle Skill and Perlica's Combo Skill, instead of just one as is the case above. Antal's Combo Skill can also be delayed to do this with no SP consumption, but this would mean giving up on an Arts Burst for weapon set triggers.
 Note that the "Final Strike" here does not indicate that it is the only Final Strike, as depending on where you are in Basic Attack strings, it's likely that a Final Strike may occur between Arclight's Ultimate and the one indicated.
 It's fine if not every Electrification is consumed by Arclight's Battle Skill, as SP economy may not allow for it. So long as there are enough Battle Skills being used to fuel Avywenna's Ultimate (and there is SP left for her own Battle Skill), it's enough.
 Shifting the Finisher to the start of the stagger period can work too, as the SP recovery it provides could sustain additional Battle Skill casts to give more Ultimate Energy if required.
